claims.text: At stage-2 Product is in Domain/Entities.cs next to Order; DonHangDbContext maps products next to orders; EfProductRepository and ProductCache are in DonHang.Infrastructure; AddDonHangInfrastructure registers IOrderRepository and ProductCache in one method.

At stage-3 DonHang.Catalog contains Product, CatalogDbContext (maps Product to table products), EfProductRepository, ProductCache and CatalogModule; CatalogModule.AddCatalogModule registers CatalogDbContext, IConnectionMultiplexer, EfProductRepository, IProductRepository (ProductCache) and ICatalog.

At stage-3 Program.cs calls AddCatalogModule(connectionString, redisConfiguration), AddDonHangInfrastructure(connectionString) and AddScoped<OrderService>(); only AddCatalogModule receives redisConfiguration. ProductsController and OrdersController are in DonHang.Api/Controllers.

At stage-3 Ordering's model and rules (Order, OrderService) are in DonHang.Domain, its storage in DonHang.Infrastructure; STAGE.md names both as the Ordering module. Infrastructure references Domain (and Catalog); Domain references none.

claims.text: C# access levels (public, internal, private…) are defined by type and by assembly (project); no access level refers to folders, so a folder does not restrict which code in the same project can use a class.

AddDonHangInfrastructure: stage-2 takes redisConfiguration, registers IOrderRepository, IConnectionMultiplexer, EfProductRepository, IProductRepository (ProductCache); stage-3 takes only connectionString, keeps IOrderRepository, drops the rest; comment: those are Catalog's own registrations.
git show <rev>:<path> prints the content of that file as it is at the given revision, such as a tag.
Ordering is Đơn Hàng's core domain and the product list a supporting subdomain, as classified in design.l3.subdomains.

Each module should pick the inside design its subdomain needs: a rules project for a module with no rules holds classes with nothing to guard; dropping the dependency rule from a module with rules loses their separation from storage.
Splitting by layer puts a slice of every context into every project, so a change to one context touches code shared with others; a 'modules' layer stacked on top does not fix that.
